head: 6fb88c89ff61392bb85a4b7be967925db28e3409
summary:
Attempt 40 closes O-027 the way the disposition allowed, and I found nothing new worth filing.

What changed (diff 2d6962c..6fb88c8):
- The window's MinHeight goes from 400 to 600, its default height (MainWindow.xaml:5), so it can no longer be made shorter than the height at which B-007 passes.
- The Grid comment (MainWindow.xaml:37-50) now says only what holds: the floor fits from about 580 px up, the guarantee is at the default width with one line of drive buttons, and the MinWidth of 560 is not covered.
- docs/design/SL-039-live-results.md:71-76 matches it.
- The hook gains a `size` mode and FSA_HOOK_MINHEIGHT=1, for watch and expand only, refused otherwise. Both set Height to MinHeight in a Window Loaded class handler before the window's own OnLoaded starts the scan.
- B-007 now runs its four endings (Completed and Cancelled, unreadable list closed and opened) again at the window's MinHeight, and CheckSized asserts the hook's 'sized' line.

I grepped src, docs, tests/window and eng. Nothing else still refers to the old 400 px minimum or the 560x400 size.

What I ran:
- WindowCases -Case All: all 25 non-network cases pass. Every B-007 MinHeight run logged 'sized height=600 minHeight=600', and TopLevelList was 31.26 px with the unreadable list closed and 19.26 px opened, all in view.
- HookCases H-001 and H-002: pass.
- `eng/dotnet.ps1 test`: 181 of 181 pass.
- rules-parity: AGREE.
- Fitness: all 29 rules hold.

The departures are declared: 600 rather than the measured ~581 px zero point, and the width case measured but not fixed. They are listed in drift together with what the next reader should know.

cases.evidence: NoRowComesFromALink asserts EntryKind.Link for all three links.

AStoppedScanListsOnlyWhatItRead, B-005, and B-007's Cancelled runs at both heights.

B-003 and B-007 feed the full list beside a filled unreadable list, closed and opened, beside SL-039's results list, at 880x600 and at the window's MinHeight, which is now the same height. The window's MinWidth of 560 is not exercised by any case; the builder measured it (see drift).
The design marks this case material:false, and no test feeds a probed file. The deferral still holds: LargestFiles.cs is unchanged and never reads Flags.

drift: Declared, and left to the open window-size question for design-slice: the MinWidth of 560 is not covered. The builder measured at 560x600: with a Cancelled scan and the unreadable list open, LargestFilesList is clipped (24 px, not in view); with a Completed scan and the list open, TopLevelList keeps 3.3 px. The XAML comment at MainWindow.xaml:37-50 says so.

MinHeight 600 equals the default Height, so B-007's four 'at MinHeight' runs currently lay out exactly as its default-size runs do. They catch only a future lowering of MinHeight. CheckBothLists passes on inView alone, which is any height above 0: after an ending SL-039's results list is 31.26 px closed and 19.26 px opened, less than one of its two-line rows, and the builder notes 581-599 px would pass at a fraction of a pixel.

The window can no longer be shorter than 600 DIPs. That fits the owner's 1920x1080 display at 100% (U-001), but not the work area of a 768-px-tall display at 125% scaling or more (about 582 DIPs). Non-100% DPI is already on validate's not-reached list.

Still standing from earlier reviews: on a small tree the outcome row's 316 px floor leaves about 105 px of blank space above a results list held at 31 px. The comment inside OutcomePanel (MainWindow.xaml:91-95) says that, opened, each list 'scrolls inside its own share', but UnreadableList still has MaxHeight=200. The plants.json F17 note still cites Scanner.cs:267, whereas the raw read is now at :281.
